about.title: Pico Rivera Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Medical malpractice cases are different from most injury claims, and that's especially true here in Pico Rivera, where residents often rely on a mix of local clinics and larger Los Angeles County medical centers for care. When a diagnosis is missed, a surgery goes sideways, or medication is administered incorrectly, families are left trying to understand what happened and whether the outcome could have been prevented. California's MICRA law adds extra layers most people never expect to face, including a 90-day pre-suit notice and a requirement that a qualified medical expert review the case. LawProactive doesn't practice law ourselves. We simply connect Pico Rivera residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney who can evaluate the medical records, explain the MICRA timeline, and help determine whether the care fell below an acceptable standard. A poor outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice, so an informed review matters.

items.title: MICRA Deadlines Move Fast
items.desc: California generally allows one year from discovering the harm and no more than three years from the injury, plus a required 90-day pre-suit notice before filing. Missing these windows can end a claim before it starts.

items.title: Non-Economic Damages Are Capped, But the Cap Rises
items.desc: MICRA sets a statutory limit on non-economic damages that increases annually, so understanding the current figure matters for evaluating a case.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Required
items.desc: California generally requires a qualified medical expert to weigh in on whether the standard of care was breached, which is why connecting with an attorney experienced in these cases matters.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, you have one year from when you discovered (or reasonably should have discovered) the injury, but no more than three years from the date it occurred. There's also a mandatory 90-day notice period before a lawsuit can be filed. An attorney can help sort out which deadline applies to your specific facts.

items.question: Is a bad medical outcome automatically malpractice?
items.answer: No. California law recognizes that not every complication or unexpected result means a provider was negligent. A claim typically requires showing the care fell below an accepted medical standard, which is why a qualified expert review is almost always needed.

items.question: Do I need to have been treated at a Pico Rivera facility to use this service?
items.answer: No. While many of the people we connect with attorneys were treated locally, whether at community clinics or larger Los Angeles County medical centers, the free connection service is available regardless of which facility provided the care in question.
